final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record. The response appropriately narrows the claim and concedes the key limiting facts, but that narrowing is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the unresolved issue is not merely a disclosure note or residual risk; it is an unsatisfied compliance predicate. The admissible evidence shows the affected health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed and below target, the rollout does not exclude it, and there is no approved risk acceptance that addresses that exposure. Under the stated policy text, rollback, small-percentage rollout, dashboards, and monitoring do not remove the disclosure duty or cure the launch condition when the affected segment remains exposed. Public guidance on monitoring and model-card content may support documenting and managing the limitation, but it does not override the internal policy requirement. On this record, certification now remains inconsistent with policy.
remaining_concerns: The health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by tenant and does not exclude the affected use case.
There is no approved risk acceptance covering the exposed health-plan benefits support segment; the draft is unsigned and omits that exposure.
Policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout controls, rollback capability, and monitoring do not satisfy the policy predicate while the affected segment remains exposed.
